text: One hot summer afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> As a black thunderstorm was coming up. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom was about to ruin a poor land speculator. <break time="0.8s" /> Who begged him for a few more months. <break time="0.8s" /> You have made so much money out of me. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the speculator. <break time="0.8s" /> And at these words. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom lost both his patience and his piety. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil take me. <break time="0.8s" /> Said he. <break time="0.8s" /> If I have made a farthing. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then there were three loud knocks. <break time="0.8s" /> At the street door. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Tom stepped out. <break time="0.8s" /> There stood the dark man. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding a black horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom, I have come for you. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the visitor gruffly. <break time="0.8s" /> And never was a sinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Taken more by surprise. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom shrank back. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was too late. <break time="0.8s" /> For he had left his little Bible in his coat pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And his big one buried under the mortgage on his desk. <break time="0.8s" /> The dark man lifted him like a child. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the saddle. <break time="0.8s" /> And away they galloped toward the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> The thunder roaring all around them. <break time="0.8s" /> Afterward his bonds and mortgages were found burned to ashes. <break time="0.8s" /> His iron chest held only wood chips. <break time="0.8s" /> And his house burned to the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Such was the end of Tom Walker. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose ghost, it is said. <break time="0.8s" /> Still haunts the swamp on stormy nights. <break time="0.8s" /> Riding a horse in his white cap.
